pages.text: $(bold)Speed Upgrade Module:$(reset) increases miner speed and energy consumption.$(br2)$(li)Each block: mining progress +12.5%, energy cost +10% per tick$(li)Cap by controller tier: Basic 8 / Advanced 16 / Super 24 / Ultimate 32 (see next page)$(br2)At maximum on an Ultimate miner this is rate ×5 at ×4.2 power draw (base 2,000 energy/tick rises to 8,400). Higher tiers consume more power, so the grid must be able to supply it before installation.

$(bold)Fortune Upgrade Module:$(reset) increases the number of items per cycle.$(br2)$(li)Each block: +1 item per cycle$(li)Cap equals the Storage cap, one quarter of the Speed cap: Basic 2 / Advanced 4 / Super 6 / Ultimate 8 (see next page)$(br2)At maximum on an Ultimate miner, every cycle yields a fixed 9 items (the type is still determined by the weight table). It adds no power cost, which is efficient for stockpiling bulk ores such as coal, iron and copper.

$(bold)Storage Upgrade Module:$(reset) increases the controller's energy capacity.$(br2)$(li)Each block: energy capacity +50% (applied to the tier's base capacity)$(li)Cap equals the Fortune cap, one quarter of the Speed cap: Basic 2 / Advanced 4 / Super 6 / Ultimate 8 (see next page)$(br2)At maximum this gives capacity ×2 / ×3 / ×4 / ×5: Basic 1M → 2M, Ultimate 50M → 250M.$(br2)$(bold)Installation:$(reset) modules are blocks placed into any U slot (upgrade-frame position), replacing an empty frame. The controller re-counts every 20 ticks, so additions and removals apply immediately. Modules are not tier-specific; the same blocks work on all four controllers, but anything beyond the current tier's cap has no effect.

$(bold)Mining Modes:$(reset) open the controller interface and select the Normal or Silk button on the right.$(br2)Normal mode: yields refined minerals (coal, raw iron, raw copper, etc.) and fortune applies in full; at maximum this is 9 items per cycle.$(br2)Silk (precise) mode: yields the raw ore blocks themselves (iron ore, diamond ore, etc.), which must be smelted or processed manually; fortune upgrades count at 1/3 in this mode (one extra per 3 blocks, rounded down; configurable).$(br2)Silk mode is used to stockpile ore blocks for a custom line or smelting; Normal mode is used to obtain finished minerals directly.

$(bold)Caps by controller tier:$(reset)$(br2)$(bold)Speed$(reset): Basic 8 → Advanced 16 → Super 24 → Ultimate 32 blocks, giving a maximum mining rate of ×2 / ×3 / ×4 / ×5.$(br2)$(bold)Storage and Fortune$(reset): both are one quarter of the Speed cap, i.e. Basic 2 / Advanced 4 / Super 6 / Ultimate 8.$(br2)The frame has 48 U slots in total, but a lower-tier controller honours only the lower cap, so maximum values require a controller upgrade. Storage and Fortune share one cap, so a choice is required between speed, energy capacity and ore yield.
Details of the U-slot layout are in Miner Structure and performance differences are in Miner Tiers; the tier and power grid are the primary factors.
